{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantitatively compares preclinical efficacy measures (IC50, TGI) with human clinical outcomes (drug approval status) for lung cancer drugs, calculating concordance statistics like AUC values and odds ratios.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "The goal was to identify features of preclinical experiments or values of efficacy parameters that might predict a drug's success in clinical testing.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "A Systematic Review of the Efficacy of Preclinical Models of Lung Cancer Drugs.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "We studied only drugs that had exhibited statistically significant efficacy in preclinical testing... conducted either in cell lines, or murine models",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "For mouse model experiments was tumor growth inhibition (TGI) calculated as (tumor volume or weight of treated mice in mm 3 –tumor volume or weight of control mice in mm 3 )/tumor volume or weight of control mice in mm 3 at the end of the follow-up period.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The outcome variable for each analysis was drug approval status, scored as approved or failed. Independent variables were IC50 and TGI."
}
